----------------------------------------------------------------
The row universe is defined by one declared admission rule (curation.json decision_log "Strict admission gating"; draft table_title): "the school's OWN Wikipedia article must itself foreground a single founder (NOT just the per-person article)." Six schools were excluded for failing it. Verified against the ledes, the rule is NOT applied consistently.

- Advaita Vedanta (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advaita_Vedanta, lede sent.1 + body): lede = "a Hindu tradition of Vedanta..."; Shankara is "the most prominent exponent of the Advaita Vedānta tradition" and later a "systematizer." Correctly excluded.

Included rows — SAME pattern present, yet admitted:
- Yoga (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yoga_(philosophy), lede sent.1-3): "Yoga philosophy is one of the six major important schools of Hindu philosophy, though it is only at the end of the first millennium CE that Yoga is mentioned as a separate school of thought... A systematic collection of ideas of Yoga is found in the Yoga Sutras of Patanjali." The lede presents Patanjali as author of a "systematic collection" — systematizer/compiler, NOT "the founder." Same grounds that excluded Advaita Vedanta. The curation itself writes Patanjali as "the systematizer / founder" — using the disqualifying word.
- Mimamsa (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mimamsa, lede): lede defines the word/tradition and names NO founder. Jaimini appears only as "A key text of the Mīmāṁsā school is the Mīmāṁsā Sūtra of Jaimini" — author of the key text, not a foregrounded founder. Fails the lede rule.
- Nyaya (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyaya, lede sent.1-2): lede defines the school and its logic contributions; names NO founder. Akshapada Gautama is introduced only in a later "Foundational Text" section as composer of the Nyaya Sutras (dated "between the 6th century BCE and the 2nd century CE"). Fails the lede rule; curation hedges "associated with the Nyaya Sutras."

Effect on scope: the admission rule is the load-bearing definition of the 18-row universe (claim_type=candidate_rebuild rests entirely on it). Applied consistently under the strict lede rule, at least Yoga, Mimamsa, Nyaya would be EXCLUDED on the same grounds as Advaita Vedanta -> universe ~15, not 18. Applied under the looser standard actually used (founder named anywhere in the article/infobox), Daoism/Laozi (infobox "Founder: Laozi") and others would re-qualify -> universe grows. Either way the membership and the hardcoded "18" change. This is a scope-BLOCKING finding under the skill's Cardinality/Partition rule (one convention must be applied; here two are mixed to hit a target count).

Recommendation (pkdb-curation repair): pick ONE convention and re-derive. FINDING 2 — "Origin Region" is asserted as "per-school-article-lede foregrounded geographic origin," but for the MAJORITY of sampled rows the lede contains NO geographic origin; several staged origins are curator scalarizations and one (Buddhism) appears in no cited source. (factual + scope, BLOCKING)
----------------------------------------------------------------
The curation (normalization_decisions, collection_summary origin_region_format, and every per_school_entries region_grounding note) repeatedly claims Origin Region = the article-lede foregrounded origin. Checking ledes directly, this is false for most rows:
- Buddhism (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buddhism, lede): "It arose in the eastern Gangetic plain... in the 5th century BCE"; lede says "Indian religion" / "ancient India" — NEVER "Northern India." Staged "Northern India" is a curator paraphrase (curation admits "per the geographic specificity of the Magadha region") and appears in no cited text. (factual: value not in cited source.)
- Neoplatonism (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neoplatonism, lede): lede gives NO origin ("emerged in the 3rd century AD"). Plotinus ("father of Neoplatonism") + his move to Rome to teach are body text; Alexandria is where he STUDIED under Ammonius Saccas. Staged "Alexandria, Roman Egypt" is a curator judgment over Rome, from body not lede. (factual + scope.)
- Phenomenology (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenomenology_(philosophy), lede): lede names NO founder and NO origin. "Germany" (Göttingen/Freiburg) is body context; Husserl was Austrian-born. Not lede-foregrounded. (scope.)
- Epicureanism (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epicureanism, lede): "founded in 307 BCE and based upon the teachings of Epicurus, an ancient Greek philosopher." NO city in lede; Athens is in History section.
- Avicennism (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avicennism, lede): "established by Avicenna." NO origin; Persia/Iran from infobox/body. Staged "Persia" not lede-foregrounded.
- Platonism (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Platonism, lede): "the philosophy of Plato and philosophical systems closely derived from it" — no founder-as-school-founder, no 4th-c date, no Athens; Academy/Athens in History section.
- Cartesianism (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cartesianism, lede): names Descartes as the system's originator + "seventeenth century thinkers," but France NOT in lede.
Only Stoicism (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stoicism) carries founder+place near the lede: "Stoicism was founded in the ancient Agora of Athens by Zeno of Citium around 300 BCE."

Why blocking, not hygiene: the curation's central honesty claim — repeated per-row — is that every cell is "article-lede foregrounded." That is demonstrably untrue for Origin Region across most rows, partly untrue for Founder (Finding 1), and for periods (Findings 1, 5). Values may be defensible against the FULL article, but the asserted grounding STANDARD ("lede") does not match the evidence, and at least one value (Buddhism "Northern India") is a paraphrase in no cited text. For a candidate_rebuild instance whose defensibility rests on faithful article grounding, this is a coverage/grounding defect to resolve before registration. (factual core: Buddhism origin unsourced; scope: grounding standard overstated column-wide.)

Recommendation: (a) downgrade the grounding claim from "lede-foregrounded" to "article-grounded (lede OR infobox OR History)" throughout curation, AND fix Buddhism origin to a sourced value ("ancient India" / "eastern Gangetic plain"); or (b) restrict to rows whose lede genuinely carries the origin (likely only Stoicism). (a) is the lighter honest fix.

FINDING 4 — operation_type=`join` mislabels a single-entity-per-row lookup; source_count=19 counts a non-row-defining master. (structural, NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE; source_count sub-point SUGGESTION)
----------------------------------------------------------------
operation_type: `join` IS in the allowed vocabulary (curation_ui/app.py OPERATION_TYPES = [join, union, intersect, projection, union+filter, filter, aggregation]; mirrored in artifact-contract.md and curation_protocol.md §7), so it passes the vocab check. BUT the structural primitive is wrong: each row's Founder/Period/Origin all come from ONE per-school article; there is no genuine join across two source TABLES on a shared key producing rows. The master "List of philosophies" is explicitly "universe-discovery only, NOT row-defining," so it is not a join input either. This is a single-source-per-row multi-column attribute lookup = `projection` (contract maps `projection` -> "single-source multi-column SELECT, no filter"); given the qualitative curator-bound WHERE, `filter` is also arguable. The db_analog writes a two-table JOIN (philosophical_schools JOIN founders) that does not match the actual one-article-per-row construction. Recommend operation_type=`projection` and a db_analog without the fictitious founders-table join. (Does not change rows, but mislabels the primitive for per-type analysis.)

source_count: curation_protocol.md §7 defines source_count as "number of implicit source tables required." The master is declared NOT row-defining, so by the protocol's own definition it is not a required source table — making 19 overstate row-defining tables (honest count = 18). Counter: artifact-contract Consistency Check requires `source_count == len(source_urls)`, and the master URL is in source_urls, so 19 preserves that invariant. Genuine protocol tension, not a clean error. Recommend keeping 19 to satisfy len(source_urls) but add the prescribed inline `Roles:` block labelling source_urls[0]=`universe` (discovery-only) vs the 18 `value` rows. The source_count question is a SUGGESTION the next curator can decide either way; the operation_type=projection switch is the substantive fix.

Source Roles hygiene: curation describes roles in prose (master=universe-discovery; 18 per-school=value) but does not use the prescribed inline `Roles:` block per artifact-contract §Source Roles. Minor.

FINDING 5 — Period bucketing has a defensible-but-inconsistent edge and one date that fights its neighbor. (factual, NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE)

- Epicureanism staged "c. late 4th century BCE"; lede says "founded in 307 BCE" (307 BCE is late 4th c. BCE — defensible). Stoicism staged "c. 3rd century BCE"; lede says "around 300 BCE." The two foundings are ~7 years apart yet land in different century buckets, which drives their relative sort order. Article-defensible per the TEXT-categorical decision, but worth a curator note.
- Yoga period "c. 2nd century BCE": the Yoga lede foregrounds Yoga as "a separate school of thought" only "at the end of the first millennium CE"; "2nd century BCE" is the Patanjali-text date, not the school-as-separate-school date — Finding-1 systematizer ambiguity bleeding into the period column. (Hygiene given Finding 1 already blocks Yoga.)
- Nyaya "c. 6th century BCE": foundational-text range is "6th c. BCE to 2nd c. CE"; choosing the earliest endpoint is a scalarization of a wide range. Defensible as TEXT but worth noting.

FINDING 6 — Hardcoded "18" in table_title leaks cardinality. (scope, NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE)
----------------------------------------------------------------
table_title begins "List 18 major philosophical schools...". In the LLM-as-DB framing this telegraphs the exact answer count, slightly trivializing the enumeration sub-task. For a deterministic source_defined universe a count is harmless; for a curator-bound qualitative universe where membership is the load-bearing judgment, stating "18" is more leakage but is not itself a blocker (other staged instances state counts, e.g. "top 20"). Two caveats raise it above cosmetic: (a) the "18" is contingent on Finding 1's unresolved rule, so the number may be wrong; (b) "major" is an explicitly qualitative/curator-bound predicate, so pinning a precise count to a fuzzy predicate is in tension. Recommend dropping the count to "List the major philosophical schools..." OR keeping it only after Finding 1 settles the universe.

----------------------------------------------------------------
FINDING 7 — domain=`Culture/Philosophy` uses a family/subdomain not in the taxonomy table. (structural, NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE)
----------------------------------------------------------------
datasets/pkdb_bench/docs/domain_taxonomy.md lists 16 families; there is NO `Philosophy` subdomain under `Culture` and no top-level Philosophy family. Closest listed homes would be `Religion/*` ("theology, religious figures") or `Society/*`. HOWEVER the taxonomy explicitly says domain is free text, prefers the closest `Family/Subdomain`, and "do not invent a new top-level family unless none fits" — `Culture/Philosophy` reuses the existing `Culture` family with a natural subdomain, which the doc's audit guidance treats as SUGGESTION/hygiene at most (value present, not misleading). The draft _extraction_notes claim "Culture/Philosophy existing subdomain" is inaccurate (not pre-listed) but harmless. Not a blocker. Recommend keeping `Culture/Philosophy` (acceptable) or aligning to `Religion/Philosophy`/`Society/Philosophy` if stratification prefers an existing family — a curator call.

----------------------------------------------------------------
Wiki-family source discovery pass (bounded)
----------------------------------------------------------------
The instance correctly identifies that no single Wikipedia "List of major philosophical schools with founders" page exists — the master "List of philosophies" is a heterogeneous cross-scheme enumeration (by tradition / century / subject), which is exactly why candidate_rebuild is the honest claim_type. I checked for a more direct list page (List of schools of philosophy, Index/Outline of philosophy) — these are link indexes, not founder/period/origin tables, so they would not supply row values. No missing row-defining source found; the per-school articles are the correct value sources. No new BLOCKING source-discovery finding. (The pass instead surfaced that the per-school ledes under-support the asserted grounding standard — captured in Findings 1, 2, 5.)

----------------------------------------------------------------
LLM-knowable fit / benchmark value
----------------------------------------------------------------
Content is strongly LLM-knowable (canonical philosophy facts, pre-cutoff). Qualitative category fit is good once the universe rule is consistent. Entity class (philosophical-schools / abstract-categories) is distinct from the sibling `major_western_philosophers_primary_works` (people entity class), so it adds genuine variety. The instance is worth saving — the defects are about rule consistency and grounding honesty, not topic fit.
